clue.text: Gift dispatched in advance?

definitions.meaning: something given to someone, a gift
sent off beforehand, the question mark flagging the playful split

explanation.surface: A present posted early so it arrives before the birthday.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: split the word as 'pre-sent' and it means sent ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something handed over freely to someone is a gift.

clue.text: Regret discourteous daughter leaving

indicators.note: leaving says the daughter's letter departs from the word for discourteous

explanation.surface: A parent regrets that their impolite daughter has walked out.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to rue something is to regret it bitterly.

clue.text: Quiet, one walked on as dismissive gesture

parts.note: SH is the call for quiet
a rug is a floor covering that people walk on

explanation.surface: Someone quietly treated as a doormat responds with a dismissive gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising the shoulders to show indifference or dismissal is the gesture meant.

clue.text: We hear Sir hits places of entertainment

indicators.note: we hear says the words are judged by their sound, not their spelling

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir; to club someone is to hit them

explanation.surface: Reports that a titled gentleman has been lashing out at people.
explanation.definitionFit: Late-night venues for dancing and drinks are a kind of entertainment place.

clue.text: Initially attempt to oppose powers above

indicators.note: initially says take the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: An attempt to stand against the powers that rule from on high.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something on top of another thing is above it.

clue.text: Part of plant where number exercise endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly says the word for exercise loses its final letter

parts.note: a drill is a training exercise

explanation.surface: A gardening note on the part of a plant where one does a set of exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendril is the slender coiling shoot by which a climbing plant clings, so a part of it.

clue.text: Proper sci-fi film — I'm ecstatic at first, when many watch

parts.note: the letters of the contraction, without its apostrophe

indicators.note: at first says only the opening letter of ecstatic is used

explanation.surface: A prim viewer delighted that a sci-fi film is showing in the busy evening slot.
explanation.definitionFit: Prime time is the evening TV period with the largest audience, when the most viewers tune in.

clue.text: Nobles open at heart, eager to change

indicators.note: at heart says take the central letters of the word open
to change says the letters of eager are rearranged

explanation.surface: Aristocrats who are open-minded at heart and eager for reform.
explanation.definitionFit: The peerage is the body of peers, the titled nobility collectively.

clue.text: Iron block found in Roman villa

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An archaeologist's report of a metal block unearthed at a Roman villa.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith hammers metal on this heavy iron block.

clue.text: Urban area series my Ed reworked

indicators.note: reworked says the letters of these words are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A writer tells of an editor reworking a set of articles.
explanation.walkthrough: MERSEYSIDE is the metropolitan county around Liverpool in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Liverpool conurbation is a large built-up region, so an urban area.

clue.text: Amusing, like flighty slights

definitions.meaning: cheerful and not serious, meant to entertain
both these words have the letters LIGHT at their heart: f-light-y and s-light-s

explanation.surface: A wry observation that small social snubs are frivolous and amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: each of 'flighty' and 'slights' has LIGHT at its centre, so both are, in a sense, 'light' at heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Something carefree and playful in tone is entertaining rather than serious.

clue.text: Learner confused — oh ask pro! Hurry!

parts.note: L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

indicators.note: confused says the letters of these words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A muddled beginner urged to ask an expert, and quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: the phrase is an order to be quick about it.

clue.text: Official from Honolulu's no coward on reflection

indicators.note: on reflection says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A diplomat in Hawaii is declared, after some thought, not to be timid.
explanation.definitionFit: A consul is a government official posted abroad to look after citizens' interests.

clue.text: Change course accommodating lieutenant in refuge

indicators.note: accommodating says the word for changing course holds the officer inside it

parts.note: to sheer is to swerve or change course

explanation.surface: A ship altering course to take on an officer seeking safety.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a place of protection from danger or weather.

clue.text: Oddly, spy I love is a girl

indicators.note: oddly says take the first, third, fifth and so on letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A spy confesses that the woman he loves is just a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Sylvia is a girl's name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: Male sensibly rearranged factory feature

indicators.note: rearranged says the letters of these words are reordered

explanation.surface: A man sensibly reorganising the layout of a factory floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A production line where work passes from station to station is a characteristic of a factory.

clue.text: Opening within chain letter

indicators.note: within says the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An opening line found inside a chain letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An inlet is a narrow opening of water into the coast, or an aperture letting something in.

clue.text: Finished a dish of macaroni?

explanation.surface: Someone has polished off a plate of macaroni.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: macaroni is one kind of the food.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaroni is a type of Italian noodle dough, so a dish of it is an example of this food.

clue.text: Give false information to girl, say, deal off

indicators.note: say tells us to take the word for girl by its sound, giving the prefix pronounced the same way

parts.note: Miss is a title for a girl or young woman

indicators.note: off says the letters of deal are out of order

explanation.surface: A dealer who tricks a young woman with a dodgy hand of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' turns MISS into the prefix MIS-, which is pronounced the same; 'off' rearranges DEAL to LEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to lead someone astray by telling them untruths.

clue.text: Wimbledon winner unreachable

parts.note: a tennis serve that wins the point outright because the receiver cannot get a racket to it

explanation.surface: A tennis champion so dominant that no rival can catch them.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a champion player; the winner meant is a single point-winning serve.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, a serve the opponent cannot touch wins the point outright.

clue.text: Left harbour

definitions.meaning: the left-hand side of a ship, looking forward
a town or haven where ships dock

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are nautical: the larboard side of a vessel, and a place where vessels shelter.

clue.text: Apprehension about the quill

indicators.note: about says the word for apprehension goes round the other word

explanation.surface: A nervous writer clutching their pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A quill is a large bird's plume, the kind once cut into a pen.
